key_insight: The PAGE framework uses AI to parse, annotate, and compare comics at archive scale, enabling new quantitative studies of visual storytelling across American comics and Japanese manga.
engineering_relevance: It shows how vision-language models and structured annotation pipelines can transform large scanned archives into searchable, analyzable datasets for research, accessibility, and preservation.
method: Parse every page into panels, text, and bibliographic records
Annotate pages with a codebook-guided vision-language model
Ground model outputs with human annotation and estimate trends controlling for publisher and genre
evidence_signal: The framework was demonstrated on 3,929 American comic books (1938–1956) and 87 volumes of Japanese manga across three studies, with human-checked evaluation for at least one task.
watch_item: Results depend on model coding quality and human-grounded annotation, so bias or errors in panel/text interpretation could propagate at archive scale.
paper_title: Studying Comics at Scale with Artificial Intelligence: The PAGE Framework and Three Studies of American Comics and Japanese Manga
